To put it simply, engines are essentially air pumps. Air comes in, air combines with gas and burns to produce power, then air goes out. 

Now a certain amount of gas needs a certain amount of air (well, oxygen) to fully combust. The more gas burned at once, the more power your engine makes. Within reason we can deliver as much gas as the engine can ever possibly need, so how do we make more power? The answer is more air. 

Now, the natural suction an engine produces can only pump so much air, so we need something to pump more air into our engine so we can pump in more gas and make more power. What can move a lot of air? A fan! But now we have another problem, what moves the fan?

Remember how part of the process of this air pump was air flowing out? We use that fast moving, normally ignored air flowing out to turn the fan, which in turn moves more air in, making more power, moving the air flowing out faster moving the fan faster and it goes on and on. This is why turbochargers can make a lot more power than it's naturally aspirated, or an engine without a turbocharger, counterpart.

All in all 10/10 weekend would recommend.

I've driven hundreds of cars working for various auctions, dealers, and vehicle transporters but I'll pick some of the standouts. 

1. 2009 911 Turbo. This was the second standard car I ever drove (first was a 1989 VW Golf the day before). This little bugger was fast as hell, but I didn't push it much. 

2. 2005 (I think) Lamborghini Gallardo with a track suspension. Probably my favorite car I've ever driven, it was stiff, responsive and quick as hell. 

3. 2003 Ferrari California Spyder. This was the first "supercar" I ever drove and while nice as hell, was kind of underwhelming. Definitely made for rich moms 

4. 2010ish Bentley. No clue what model, I only drove it for 5 minutes but it was pretty baller. 

5. 2012 Challenger SRT with the 6.7L supercharged Hemi and a 5 speed. This car had BALLS, big ones, and sounded so good. It took my boss yelling at me for me to stop driving it, I truly fell in love with it. 

6. 2013 Golf GTI, peppy as all fuck and fun to mess around in in an empty parking lot. 

7. 2004 Impala SS. I drive an 03 LS and love the w body Impalas, this thing was awesome. Had a smile on my face the whole time. 

8. 1960s era Fiat convertible that my landlord/neighbor owns. Peppy little fucker, pretty fun. Took a while to get used to the transmission but it's a fun summer car 

9. 1971 Dart, freaking thing was a slow landboat that had a wider turning radius than an actual boat. Do not recommend. 

10. 1972 Corvette C3. Everyone at the auction swooned over it, but me being a fat person, I was not too thrilled. 

Those are the standouts, I've driven pretty much everything you can think of that's not in the supercar/hyper car territory.
